title: Find a Standard Regression Equation from Data
description: Turn information from a table, graph, or word problem into points, enter the points in a Desmos table, and use the Regression button to fit a linear, quadratic, or exponential equation.

questions.stem_html: The table gives values of a linear function. What is the slope of this function?
questions.explanation_html: Fit a line to the (x, y) pairs. The change in y divided by the change in x is 4. The model is \(y=4x+8\).
questions.variation: Recover a linear model from table points

questions.stem_html: The table follows a quadratic model. What is the coefficient of x² in the model?
questions.explanation_html: Fit a quadratic to all the table points. The model is \(y=2x^{2}+x+5\), giving the requested value 2.
questions.variation: Fit a quadratic and report its coefficient or prediction

questions.stem_html: The table follows an exponential model. What is the output at x = 4?
questions.explanation_html: The output is multiplied by 2 each time x increases by 1 and starts at 7. The exponential fit is \(y=7(2)^x\); evaluating it gives 112.
questions.variation: Recover an exponential model and make a prediction

questions.stem_html: A quadratic function f has vertex \((4,6)\) and \(f(2)=18\). What is \(f(7)\)?
questions.explanation_html: The point opposite x = 2 across the axis x = 4 is x = 6, with the same output. Fit a quadratic to those two points and the vertex to obtain \(f(x)=3(x-4)^2+6\). Its output at 7 is 33.
questions.variation: Use vertex symmetry to form enough points for a quadratic fit

questions.stem_html: A pump fills a tank at a steady rate. A linear model gives an output of 33 at time 2 and 61 at time 6. What output does the model predict at time 8?
questions.explanation_html: Enter (2, 33) and (6, 61) as table points. The linear fit is \(y=7x+19\). At time 8, it predicts 75.
questions.variation: Turn conditions in words into ordered pairs and a linear prediction

questions.stem_html: Use the linear model represented by the table to predict y when x is 10.
questions.explanation_html: The linear fit is \(y=-3x+37\). Evaluating it at x = 10 gives 7.
questions.variation: Recover a linear model from table points

questions.stem_html: The table follows a quadratic model. What is the model’s output at x = 6?
questions.explanation_html: Fit a quadratic to all the table points. The model is \(y=x^{2}-4x+8\), giving the requested value 20.
questions.variation: Fit a quadratic and report its coefficient or prediction

questions.stem_html: The table follows an exponential model. What is the output at x = 5?
questions.explanation_html: The output is multiplied by 3 each time x increases by 1 and starts at 3. The exponential fit is \(y=3(3)^x\); evaluating it gives 729.
questions.variation: Recover an exponential model and make a prediction

questions.stem_html: A quadratic function f has vertex \((5,8)\) and \(f(3)=16\). What is \(f(9)\)?
questions.explanation_html: The point opposite x = 3 across the axis x = 5 is x = 7, with the same output. Fit a quadratic to those two points and the vertex to obtain \(f(x)=2(x-5)^2+8\). Its output at 9 is 40.
questions.variation: Use vertex symmetry to form enough points for a quadratic fit

questions.stem_html: A training log models the total minutes linearly. A linear model gives an output of 41 at time 3 and 89 at time 7. What output does the model predict at time 11?
questions.explanation_html: Enter (3, 41) and (7, 89) as table points. The linear fit is \(y=12x+5\). At time 11, it predicts 137.

questions.stem_html: A quadratic function f has vertex \((7,3)\) and \(f(5)=19\). What is \(f(10)\)?
questions.explanation_html: The point opposite x = 5 across the axis x = 7 is x = 9, with the same output. Fit a quadratic to those two points and the vertex to obtain \(f(x)=4(x-7)^2+3\). Its output at 10 is 39.

questions.stem_html: A download meter models the total megabytes linearly. A linear model gives an output of 98 at time 4 and 174 at time 8. What output does the model predict at time 10?
questions.explanation_html: Enter (4, 98) and (8, 174) as table points. The linear fit is \(y=19x+22\). At time 10, it predicts 212.
